title: A short story
summary: Follow and retell a short folk story in the past tense: Juha, his son and their donkey.
intro: Stories are told in the past tense, usually verb first: ذَهَبَ جُحَا (Juha went), قَالَ النَّاس (the people said). When the verb comes before a plural subject it stays singular; after it, it is plural: النَّاس قَالُوا. The links you know carry the story along: ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ (one day), ثُمَّ (then), بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ (after that), أَخِيرًا (finally).
objectives: Follow a short story told in the past tense
Retell it in order with ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ, ثُمَّ, بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ and أَخِيرًا
Keep a verb singular when it comes before its subject: قَالَ النَّاس
Say the th sounds of ذَهَبَ and ثُمَّ

realLife.title: Story time with Juha
realLife.story: At the end of the week Mr Karim reads the class a story about Juha, the joker of Arab folk tales. Sami and Layla grew up with his stories; for Daniel it is the first story he has followed all the way through in Arabic.

sentences.ar: ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ ذَهَبَ جُحَا إِلَى السُّوق.
sentences.en: One day Juha went to the market.
sentences.literal: one day went Juha to the market

sentences.en: Juha rode the donkey, and his son walked.
sentences.literal: rode Juha the donkey and walked his son

mistakes.why: In standard Arabic رَكِبَ takes its object directly, with no word for 'on': rakiba l-ḥimār, 'he rode the donkey'.

sentences.literal: said the people: poor (is) the boy

mistakes.why: A verb that comes before its subject stays singular: قَالَ النَّاس. After the subject it is plural: النَّاس قَالُوا.

sentences.ar: لَمْ يَسْمَعْ دَانْيَال عَنْ جُحَا قَبْلَ هٰذَا الْيَوْم.
sentences.en: Daniel had never heard of Juha before today.
sentences.literal: not hears Daniel about Juha before this day

sentences.en: It was a short and lovely story.
sentences.literal: it (f) was a story short and beautiful

dialogue.title: Juha and the donkey
dialogue.culture: جُحَا is the best-loved joker of Arab folk tales, wise and foolish at the same time; Egyptians call him Goha. The same character appears as Nasreddin Hodja in Turkey and Iran, and children from Morocco to Iraq grow up with his stories.

lines.ar: يَا طُلَّاب، فِي آخِرِ هٰذَا الْأُسْبُوع نَقْرَأُ قِصَّة قَصِيرَة. هَلْ سَمِعْتُمْ عَنْ جُحَا؟
lines.en: Students, to finish this week we are going to read a short story. Have you heard of Juha?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا يَا أُسْتَاذ! فِي مِصْر نُسَمِّيهِ جُحَا أَيْضًا، وَكُلُّ الْأَطْفَال يَعْرِفُونَ قِصَصَهُ.
lines.en: Of course, teacher! In Egypt we call him Juha too, and all children know his stories.

lines.ar: أَنَا لَمْ أَسْمَعْ عَنْهُ أَبَدًا. مَنْ هُوَ؟ هَلْ كَانَ رَجُلًا حَقِيقِيًّا؟
lines.en: I've never heard of him. Who is he? Was he a real man?

lines.ar: جُحَا شَخْصِيَّة قَدِيمَة وَمَشْهُورَة جِدًّا. كَانَ ذَكِيًّا، لٰكِنْ كَانَ النَّاس يَضْحَكُونَ مِنْهُ وَمَعَهُ.
lines.en: Juha is a very old and famous character. He was clever, but people used to laugh at him and with him.

lines.ar: فِي لُبْنَان أَيْضًا نَعْرِفُهُ. اِقْرَأْ لَنَا الْقِصَّة يَا أُسْتَاذ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ!
lines.en: We know him in Lebanon too. Please read us the story, teacher!

lines.ar: ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ ذَهَبَ جُحَا وَابْنُهُ إِلَى السُّوق مَعَ حِمَارِهِمَا. رَكِبَ جُحَا، وَمَشَى الْوَلَد.
lines.en: One day Juha and his son went to the market with their donkey. Juha rode, and the boy walked.

lines.ar: وَمَاذَا قَالَ النَّاس؟ أَنَا أَعْرِفُ هٰذِهِ الْقِصَّة، لٰكِنْ لَنْ أَقُولَ النِّهَايَة!
lines.en: And what did the people say? I know this story, but I won't tell you the ending!

lines.ar: قَالَ النَّاس: مِسْكِين الْوَلَد! فَنَزَلَ جُحَا وَرَكِبَ الْوَلَد، فَقَالُوا: مِسْكِين الْأَب!
lines.en: The people said: 'Poor boy!' So Juha got down and the boy rode, and they said: 'Poor father!'

lines.ar: النَّاس لَمْ يَكُونُوا رَاضِينَ أَبَدًا! وَمَاذَا فَعَلَا بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ؟
lines.en: The people were never happy! And what did the two of them do after that?

lines.ar: رَكِبَا الْحِمَار مَعًا، فَقَالُوا: مِسْكِين الْحِمَار! وَأَخِيرًا حَمَلَا الْحِمَار عَلَى ظَهْرَيْهِمَا!
lines.en: They both rode the donkey together, so the people said: 'Poor donkey!' And finally the two of them carried the donkey on their backs!

lines.ar: هَاهَا! وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ النَّاس عِنْدَمَا شَاهَدُوهُمَا؟
lines.en: Ha ha! And what did the people do when they saw the two of them?
segs: they saw the two of them

lines.ar: ضَحِكُوا كَثِيرًا! وَقَالَ جُحَا لِابْنِهِ: هُمْ لَا يَرْضَوْنَ أَبَدًا. لَا نَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ نُرْضِيَ كُلَّ النَّاس.
lines.en: They laughed a lot! And Juha said to his son: 'They are never satisfied. We can't please everyone.'

lines.ar: قِصَّة جَمِيلَة! وَهٰذِهِ أَوَّلُ قِصَّة سَمِعْتُهَا بِالْعَرَبِيَّة، وَفَهِمْتُ كُلَّ كَلِمَة!
lines.en: A lovely story! And it's the first story I've heard in Arabic, and I understood every word!

lines.ar: أَحْسَنْتُمْ يَا طُلَّاب! هٰذَا الْأُسْبُوع ذَهَبْتُمْ مَعِي إِلَى الْمَاضِي. الْوَاجِب: اُكْتُبُوا الْقِصَّة بِكَلِمَاتِكُمْ.
lines.en: Well done, students! This week you travelled into the past with me. Homework: write the story in your own words.

reading.title: Juha, his son and the donkey
reading.ar: ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ ذَهَبَ جُحَا وَابْنُهُ إِلَى السُّوق، وَمَعَهُمَا حِمَار. رَكِبَ جُحَا الْحِمَار وَمَشَى الْوَلَد، فَقَالَ النَّاس: مِسْكِين الْوَلَد! ثُمَّ رَكِبَ الْوَلَد وَمَشَى جُحَا، فَقَالُوا: مِسْكِين الْأَب! بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ رَكِبَا الْحِمَار مَعًا، فَقَالُوا: مِسْكِين الْحِمَار! أَخِيرًا حَمَلَا الْحِمَار، فَضَحِكَ كُلُّ النَّاس.
reading.en: One day Juha and his son went to the market, and they had a donkey with them. Juha rode the donkey and the boy walked, so the people said: 'Poor boy!' Then the boy rode and Juha walked, and they said: 'Poor father!' After that they both rode the donkey together, and they said: 'Poor donkey!' Finally the two of them carried the donkey, and everyone laughed.

quiz.prompt: What does this story opening mean?
What did the people say when the son rode and Juha walked?
What did Juha and his son do in the end?
options: They left the donkey at the market.

quiz.prompt: Which is correct for 'The people said…'?
What is the lesson of the story?
Which word starts with the th of 'this' (ذ)?

completion: Mabrūk! You followed a whole story in the past tense and can retell it in order. Take the week test (80% to pass) to open Week 7.
